purpose: Original fictional teaching examples. Gold and anti-gold are relative to a distinction, not high and low scores. Both sides have approved labels. These labels belong in teaching packets. They are not target answer keys.

references.title: Approve the launch copy
references.content:
From: Fictional colleague
Please approve the launch copy by April 9. We need your answer to publish the product page on time.
references.context: Fictional review on April 8; next review April 10. The reader owns approval and has not replied. This is the complete conversation.
references.label: act
references.distinction: The recipient still owes a concrete answer; the confirmation example has a later reply resolving it.

references.title: Launch copy approved
references.content:
Colleague: Please approve the launch copy by April 9.
Recipient: Approved.
Colleague: Received your approval, thank you. No further action needed.
references.context: Fictional teaching example only. No other messages or facts are implied.
references.label: skip
references.distinction: The later sent reply and acknowledgment resolve the request and add no useful new information.

references.title: Repair quote pending
references.content:
Recipient: Please send a quote for the agreed bathroom repair.
Repair company: We will send it April 12; nothing is needed from you until then.
references.context: Fictional teaching example only. No other messages or facts are implied.
references.label: read
references.distinction: A promised delivery date is useful to know, but the reader has nothing to do yet.

references.title: Last chance: spring sale
references.content: Cedar & Thread: Our optional spring clothing sale ends tonight. Shop if you want. This is a general promotion, unrelated to any existing order.
references.context: Fictional reader explicitly does not want recurring optional Cedar & Thread sale emails. Existing orders, personal asks and account issues are exceptions. This is the complete message; no obligation exists.
references.label: skip
references.distinction: Urgent marketing language does not make a task. The waiting example concerns an existing deliverable.

references.title: A small balcony garden
references.content: Small Space Garden newsletter: For a small balcony, grow herbs in containers with drainage, check the light available, and water when the soil feels dry. No reply or task is requested.
references.context: Fictional reader has asked to read practical balcony-gardening ideas. This is the whole newsletter.
references.label: read
references.distinction: The reader asked for this subject. Both are recurring mail, but only one matches the reader's interests.

references.title: Choose a weekend for the family visit
references.content: Sam: Please let me know which weekend works for the family visit by April 18. We will make plans after that; nothing needs booking this week.
references.context: Fictional assessment on April 8; next review April 10. The reader owns the choice, with no earlier preparation need or explicit priority.
references.label: act
references.distinction: A reply is still owed even when the deadline is not today.
